THE DESIGN'S ONLY CIRCULAR DEPENDENCY, RESOLVED 2026-08-23, AND IT WAS NEVER A DEPENDENCY.

`dec:exploratory-staging` and `dec:idea-do-ideas-form-a-graph-or-only-a-list` each carried a DEPENDS_ON to the other. Reading both edges settled it in minutes:

  KEPT   exploratory-staging → do-ideas-form-a-graph. Dated 2026-08-21, confidence 0.8, and carrying real evidence: exploratory-staging turns on whether ANY COMPUTATION would read the idea-kind distinction, and cluster-search over an idea's neighbourhood is a candidate for exactly that computation — so the older question cannot be settled until this one is answered. That is a genuine ordering claim.

  RETRACTED   do-ideas-form-a-graph → exploratory-staging. No date, no confidence, no evidence. Its whole content was the note *"that node asks what an idea IS; this asks what it is CONNECTED TO"* — which is not a dependency claim at all. It says the two are DIFFERENT.

⭐ AND THE SENTENCE WAS ALREADY IN THE NODE'S OWN PROSE, WORD FOR WORD: "DISTINCT FROM `dec:exploratory-staging`... That node is about what an idea IS; this one is about what an idea is CONNECTED TO." So the edge duplicated, in the wrong edge type, something the node already said better. Deleting it lost nothing and made a real dependency readable again.

🛑 THE VOCABULARY GAP IS THE FINDING, NOT THE CYCLE. There is NO EDGE TYPE MEANING "RELATED BUT DISTINCT" between two Decisions. `describe_schema` for that pair returns nothing that models it: DEPENDS_ON, EVOLVES_INTO, CONTRADICTS and the rest accept Decision→Decision only through a `*` wildcard on both ends. So somebody with a true and useful thing to say — "these two questions are adjacent and must not be confused" — had one honest option, prose, and one available option, a wrong edge. They took both, and the wrong edge outlived the prose in every computation that walks the graph.

⚠️ THIS IS THE SECOND OBSERVED INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE, and Anthony raised the first from another session the same day: SUPERSEDES is `Fragment → Fragment` only and has ZERO edges in this design, while sessions reaching for a replacement relation between two same-type nodes get refused and fall back to EVOLVES_INTO — which also only wildcard-accepts the pair. A third instance appeared in this session: linking two TemporalFacts, nothing models the pair either.
  ⇒ THE PATTERN: when the schema models no edge for a real relationship, the relationship does not go unrecorded. IT GETS RECORDED AS SOMETHING ELSE, and the something else is then read by every detector as if it meant what it says. A wildcard-accepted edge is not a neutral fallback; it is an assertion in the wrong vocabulary.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether to add such an edge type. That is a schema change and Anthony's call. Three instances is a pattern worth naming, not yet a mandate — and `schema/verify.yaml` already warns from its own history that widening or narrowing an endpoint list deserves scrutiny in both directions.
